cards.text: Josiah, king of Judah, has had his men repairing the temple, where Hilkiah the priest found the Book of the Law, and Josiah made a covenant before the LORD (2 Chronicles 34:8, 14, 31). Now Josiah keeps the Passover to the LORD in Jerusalem, and the Passover lamb is slaughtered on the fourteenth day of the first month. Friend, two oven timers going off at once gets me flustered, and this man is organizing a whole NATION.

cards.question: Josiah appoints the priests to their duties and ___ them in the service of the house of the LORD.

cards.text: Then Josiah turns to the Levites, the ones who taught all Israel and were holy to the LORD. He tells them to put the holy ark in the temple built by Solomon son of David king of Israel, and to serve the LORD their God and His people Israel.

cards.question: Josiah tells the Levites the ark is to be carried around on their shoulders.

cards.text: Josiah tells them to prepare by families in their divisions, following the instructions written by David and his son Solomon, and to stand in the Holy Place by the divisions of the families. Friend, that's the biggest seating chart I've ever heard of, and SOMEBODY get this man a clipboard.

cards.question: Josiah tells the Levites to slaughter the Passover lambs, consecrate themselves, and make preparations for others too. For whom?
In his instructions to the Levites, Josiah talks about carrying out the word of the LORD given by Moses.

cards.text: Now, a Passover for everybody who shows up takes animals. A LOT of animals, friend, more than all the chocolate chips I've ever owned, and I have owned a SHAMEFUL amount of chocolate chips.

cards.question: Josiah gives 30,000 lambs and goats plus 3,000 bulls for the Passover offerings. Where do they come from?

answers.text: A new tax on the people

cards.question: Josiah isn't the only one giving. His officials contribute to the people, priests and Levites too. How do they give?

cards.text: The chief officials of the house of God give the priests thousands of Passover offerings and hundreds of bulls, and the officers of the Levites do the same for the Levites. Everybody's bringing something to this one.
So the service is ready: priests in their places, Levites in their divisions, all by the king's command. Then the Passover lambs are slaughtered, and everybody's got a job.

cards.question: As the Passover lambs are slaughtered, the priests skin the animals while the Levites splatter the blood.

cards.text: They set aside the burnt offerings for the families to offer to the LORD, as it is written in the Book of Moses, and they do the same with the bulls. Then it's time to cook, which, I'm not gonna lie to you, is my FAVORITE part of anything.

cards.question: How are the Passover animals cooked, according to the regulation?
After the other holy offerings are boiled in pots, kettles and bowls, they're brought quickly to all the people.

cards.text: Everybody's been served, but the priests, the descendants of Aaron, are still offering burnt offerings and fat until nightfall. That's me on a big baking day: every batch out of the oven, and I still haven't had a single crumb.

cards.question: The priests are busy offering burnt offerings and fat until nightfall. Who makes preparations for them?

cards.text: Meanwhile, the singers, the descendants of Asaph, are at their stations.

cards.question: The singers, the descendants of Asaph, are at their stations by a king's command. Whose?

cards.text: And the gatekeepers at each gate don't need to leave their posts, because their fellow Levites make preparations for them.

So on that day the entire service of the LORD is carried out, the Passover and the burnt offerings on the altar, just as King Josiah commanded. Friend, when every job on the list gets done just like the boss said, I call that a GOOD day at work.

cards.question: Along with the Passover, the Israelites who are present observe the Feast of Unleavened Bread. For how long?
No Passover like Josiah's has been observed in Israel since the days of ___ the prophet.

cards.text: All of this happens in the eighteenth year of Josiah's reign. Hold that thought, friend, because Josiah's story isn't finished yet.
